commands.review_summary:
Adds a gateway `terminal.*` PTY protocol, terminal config, CSP/bootstrap support, a dockable ghostty-web Control UI terminal, generated Swift protocol models, tests, and a new UI dependency.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: the app resolves an active workspace agent but renders the terminal panel without it, and the panel calls `terminal.open` with only rows and columns. I did not run the UI because this was a read-only review.

target.title: feat: embedded operator terminal — gateway foundation + web Control UI (1/3)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw deployments on WSL, Docker, or remote servers have no built-in shell: to run a command alongside the assistant you switch to a separate SSH client or device, breaking the Control UI's single-pane-of-glass. This adds an embedded operator terminal — a real PTY-backed shell — to the Control UI, and lays the gateway foundation the iOS and Android apps build on next.

Closes #77362.

**PR 1 of 3** (foundation + web UI). PR 2 adds the iOS Terminal tab, PR 3 adds Android; both consume the gateway `terminal.*` protocol introduced here (served as a full-screen terminal page for their WebViews).

## Why This Change Was Made

Prior attempts informed the design:
- #28691 (closed to the stale-bot, not on merits) proved the xterm.js + per-connection PTY RPC shape works. We keep that session model but use **ghostty-web** — Ghostty's real VT core compiled to WASM (xterm.js-compatible API) — instead of xterm.js, per maintainer preference.
- #52493 was **rejected for security**: it routed shells through a generic `exec.run`, so any `operator.write` client could run `{command:"sh",args:["-c",…]}` = arbitrary RCE. We deliberately avoid that trap — the terminal is a dedicated `terminal.*` method family gated to `operator.admin`, never a general command-exec seam.

## User Impact

- A **dockable** terminal panel in the Control UI — a real bottom bar or right sidebar that reshapes the content (the chat reflows to make room; it is not an overlay), toggled with the toolbar button or **Ctrl+`**, with multiple session tabs. The bottom dock follows the shell layout, aligning to the nav rail when collapsed and spanning full width on narrow/mobile viewports.
- Each session starts in the target agent's workspace.
- **Workspace isolation mirrors the agent's own sandbox, fail-closed:** with no sandbox (`off`, the default) you get a host shell that can navigate the whole filesystem. Under `non-main` the agent's main session already runs on the host, so a host terminal is allowed there too. Only a **fully-sandboxed agent (`sandbox.mode: "all"`)** is refused rather than handed an unconfined host shell — running the terminal *inside* an active sandbox is a tracked follow-up.
- Enabled by default; `gateway.terminal.enabled: false` is a kill switch, `gateway.terminal.shell` overrides the shell. Changing `gateway.terminal.*` **restarts the gateway** (like other `gateway.*` config): the terminal drives the Control UI CSP and bootstrap availability — both fixed at document load — plus live PTYs, none of which can hot-update a connected client. The restart kills every live PTY and clients reconnect with the correct page state.

## Security

A browser-authenticated host shell is an RCE-class surface (per the #77362 review), so:
- **Admin-only.** All `terminal.*` methods (and the `terminal.data`/`terminal.exit` event streams) require `operator.admin` — the same bar as `config.set`. An authenticated admin operator can already edit config and drive agents to exec, so this adds convenience, not new authority. The Control UI mirrors this: the toolbar toggle and dock only appear for a **live, admin** connection, and the panel tears its tabs down on disconnect rather than pointing input at server-killed sessions.
- **Not `exec.run`.** Dedicated methods; no arbitrary command routing (contrast #52493).
- **Fail-closed isolation.** A fully-sandboxed agent (`sandbox.mode: "all"`) is refused, never downgraded to a host shell. Explicit agent ids are validated against the configured agent list first — an unknown id is rejected rather than silently resolved against global defaults (which would sidestep a per-agent sandbox refusal).
- **Lifecycle-bound.** Sessions are pinned to the opening connection, killed on disconnect and on gateway shutdown (process-tree kill, so child commands don't orphan); a per-gateway session cap bounds process use.
- **Scoped CSP relaxation.** ghostty-web's WASM needs `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` + `data:` in `connect-src`; these are added to the Control UI CSP **only when the terminal is enabled**, so the baseline policy stays tight. A page served while disabled reloads itself once if the flag flips on (the bootstrap refetch after the enabling restart detects it), since headers can't change on a live document.
- **Auditable.** Each open logs agent, session id, connection, and shell. **Kill switch:** `gateway.terminal.enabled: false` restarts the gateway (killing all live PTYs and reloading clients with the tight CSP); the RPC handlers also re-check config as an independent backstop and close any session that receives input while disabled.

## Architecture

- **Protocol** (`packages/gateway-protocol`): `terminal.open/input/resize/close` methods + `terminal.data/terminal.exit` events, additive; generated schema + Swift models regenerated.
- **Gateway** (`src/gateway/terminal/*`): `TerminalSessionManager` owns one `@lydell/node-pty` PTY per session and streams bytes to only the owning connection; `resolveTerminalLaunch` resolves agent → workspace → shell and enforces the fail-closed isolation rule.
- **Config**: `gateway.terminal.{enabled,shell}` with types, zod schema, labels, help; changes route through the standard `gateway.*` restart rule (no bespoke hot-reload machinery).
- **Control UI** (`ui/src/ui/terminal/*`): `<openclaw-terminal-panel>` (dockable bottom/right, resizable, session tabs) driving ghostty-web; `TerminalConnection` is the DOM-free protocol layer that subscribes to the shared gateway event stream only while sessions exist (failed opens and panel teardown release the listener, so reconnect cycles never accumulate subscriptions). ghostty-web is dynamically imported so its ~0.6 MB WASM chunk never weighs down the initial bundle. The dock publishes its footprint as CSS vars so the shell content reserves space instead of being overlaid.

## Evidence

- **Live end-to-end** (headless Chromium against a real gateway): opened the terminal from the toolbar, ran `pwd && ls && echo …` and `whoami && uname -sr` in both bottom and right docks and in a second session tab — real zsh prompt, workspace listing, and command output rendered; verified the content area shrinks (no overlap) when docked. Two integration bugs were caught and fixed this way: the Control UI CSP blocked the WASM load, and `terminal.data`/`terminal.exit` weren't in the gateway's event-scope guard so output never reached the client.
- **Unit tests**: session manager (open/input/resize/exit/disconnect/cap, concurrent-open cap, orphan-abort on disconnect-during-spawn, spawn-failure, silent dispose-all on shutdown), launch resolver (host plan, `non-main` allowed, `all` refused, shell resolution), CSP builder (wasm relaxation gated), kill switch (disabled `terminal.input`/`terminal.resize` close the session and reject; `gateway.terminal.*` config changes classify as gateway restart), UI availability predicate (gated on live connection + `operator.admin` scope + advertised method; unavailable while disconnected or for non-admin operators), UI connection layer (event routing, early-event buffering + replay for the open race, exit self-release/no-leak, unsubscribe on close/failed-open/dispose), advertised-method-order stability.
- **Responsive dock verified** headlessly against the real shell CSS: the bottom dock's left edge resolves to 258px (nav expanded), 78px (collapsed rail), and 0px (<1100px / mobile), instead of a fixed 258px that used to gap the collapsed layout and waste most of a phone viewport.
- **Reviewed** across many rounds of adversarial code review; the lifecycle was hardened for the open/exit races, the per-gateway session cap under concurrent opens, orphaned PTYs on disconnect-during-spawn, failed-open phantom tabs, tab-closed-while-open-in-flight cancellation (the fresh session is closed instead of surviving invisibly), reconnect teardown, availability gating (live admin connection, not just the server-wide advertised-method list), gateway-client listener leaks on failed opens, live light/dark theme switching (ghostty-web 0.4.0 ignores `options.theme` after `open()`, so the panel drives `renderer.setTheme` + one forced full render — verified against the dependency source), persisted dock sizes clamped to the current viewport (load, drag, and window-resize), and the responsive dock offset. The config-change path was deliberately simplified from a bespoke hot-reload action to the standard gateway restart after review showed CSP/bootstrap can't hot-update a connected client.
- `tsgo` type-checks clean (core + UI test projects); `ui:i18n:check` clean; protocol schema + Swift models regenerated and committed; dynamic imports for `ghostty-web`/`node-pty` confirmed code-split (no static-import bundling). Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm ui:build` run in CI.
